sections.title: Income tax on individuals (Schedule 1)
sections.basis: taxable income of an individual for an income year
sections.note: Income Tax Act of Bhutan 2025, in force from 1 January 2026 (section 2). The Schedule gives cumulative amounts: Nu. 10,000 at 500,000, 35,000 at 750,000, 102,500 at 1,200,000, 262,500 at 2,000,000 and 637,500 at 3,500,000.

rows.label: Employment income deduction: 15% of employment income, at most Nu. 150,000
rows.note: total employment income of a resident individual, up to Nu. 150,000. Section 44.

rows.label: Education expenses relief (own or child's education): actual expenses up to Nu. 350,000 (Nu. 50,000 without documents)
rows.note: Schedule 6, paragraph 1.

rows.label: Homeownership relief: interest on a loan for a citizen's first home, up to Nu. 200,000
rows.note: Schedule 6, paragraphs 2 and 3.

rows.label: Insurance relief: life insurance premiums up to Nu. 50,000
rows.note: Schedule 6, paragraph 4.

rows.label: Disability relief: Nu. 40,000
rows.note: Schedule 6, paragraph 6.

rows.label: Withholding by employers: rates in regulations based on the individual rates
rows.value: Employers withhold tax from employment payments at rates prescribed in regulations, based on the individual income tax rates in Schedule 1
rows.note: Sections 264-265 and Schedule 1, paragraph 7(1). The DRC withholding table for employers (2026) is a scanned PDF and is not stored.

rows.label: Rental income: deduction of 20% of gross rent for repairs and maintenance
rows.note: gross rental income from real property (with interest on qualifying loans, property tax and insurance the only other deductions). Section 74.

rows.label: Capital gains of resident individuals on private (non-business) assets: exempt
rows.value: Gains derived by a resident individual from the disposal of an asset that is not a depreciable asset, a non-depreciable asset or trading stock of a business are exempt
rows.note: Schedule 3, paragraph 6.

sections.title: Dividends, interest and payments to non-residents

rows.label: Dividends received by an individual (not a business): exempt up to Nu. 300,000 a year
rows.note: Schedule 3, paragraph 9.

rows.label: Fixed deposit interest received by an individual (not a business): exempt up to Nu. 400,000 a year (recurring and savings deposit interest fully exempt)
rows.note: Schedule 3, paragraphs 7 and 8.

rows.label: Withholding on interest and dividend payments to individuals
rows.note: interest or dividend payments with a source in Bhutan to an individual. Section 266 and Schedule 1, paragraph 7(2)(b); not on interest paid to resident financial institutions (section 268).

rows.label: Withholding on other investment returns (rents, royalties, charges, annuities)
rows.note: other investment returns of section 31(1) (rents, royalties, charges, annuities, natural resource payments) with a source in Bhutan. Section 266 and Schedule 1, paragraph 7(2)(a).

rows.label: Withholding on service fees paid to non-residents
rows.note: service fees with a source in Bhutan paid to a non-resident person. Section 269(2) and Schedule 1, paragraph 7(3)(b).

sections.title: Social insurance contributions

rows.label: NPPF contribution, employee: civil service and government agencies
rows.note: basic pay, monthly; civil service and government agencies (armed forces 15%). Of the 26% total for the civil service, 16% goes to the pension and 10% to the provident fund; the rates of the private-sector scheme are not on this page.

rows.note: Income Tax Act of Bhutan 2025, in force from 1 January 2026 (section 2). Schedule 1, paragraph 4 (the 2001 Act charged 30% on state enterprises and 25% on other companies).

rows.note: Schedule 1, paragraph 3.

rows.label: Non-residents with significant economic presence: 5% of income as final tax (22% of taxable income when filing a return)
rows.note: income of a non-resident with significant economic presence that does not file a return (final tax); 22% of taxable income if it files. Schedule 1, paragraphs 5 and 6.

rows.label: GST registration turnover threshold
rows.note: turnover in the previous twelve months (or half of it in six months, or expected turnover). Schedule II and section 57.

rows.label: Land tax
rows.note: taxable land value, each year. Property Tax Act of Bhutan 2022, section 8; concessions in Chapter 4.

rows.label: Building tax
rows.note: taxable building value, each year. Section 11.

rows.label: Vacant land tax: 15% of the land tax
rows.note: the land tax on undeveloped serviced urban land (Schedule 2 areas, two years after urban services). Sections 15 and 16.

sections.title: Freelancers, contractors and the self-employed

rows.label: Presumptive taxation of small businesses (up to Nu. 5 million, not GST-registered): taxable income is 15% of business income
rows.note: total business income of a resident individual whose income is only from a business in Bhutan, up to Nu. 5 million, not registered for GST; taxable income = 15% of total business income, then taxed at the individual rates. Schedule 2.

rows.label: Withholding on service fees paid to resident individuals (not employees)
rows.note: service fees with a source in Bhutan paid to a resident individual who is not the payer's employee. Section 269(1) and Schedule 1, paragraph 7(3)(a).

rows.label: Withholding on payments to residents for trading stock (not retail resale)
rows.note: payments to another resident person for trading stock (section 27(2)), unless the stock is sold by that person in retail. Section 269(3) and Schedule 1, paragraph 7(3)(c).

rows.label: Withholding on payments to non-residents under turnkey contracts
rows.note: payments to a non-resident under a contract for a complete and functional outcome (goods and services). Section 269(4) and Schedule 1, paragraph 7(3)(d).

rows.label: Withholding on each partner's share of partnership income
rows.note: each partner's share of partnership income. Section 170 and Schedule 1, paragraph 8.

sections.note: Self-employed contributions, withholding on payments to freelancers and contractors, simplified regimes for small businesses, and expat and digital-nomad rules.
